R449.note: Adds a per-category method whitelist checked before dispatch; only the real handler method (send) is allowed, closing the dynamic-dispatch vector without breaking any working codepath.

R450.note: can:refund,order route middleware plus an ownership-checking OrderPolicy is the correct Laravel authorization pattern and matches the stated contract exactly.

R451.note: GUID-renaming plus canonical-path validation closes the traversal vector, but it silently (well, disclosed in the write-up) discards the client-chosen filename entirely, so a legitimate admin can no longer name or later reference an uploaded template by its intended name -- a stated restriction the original code did not have.

R452.note: Minimal, correct addition of secure: true; no other observable change.

R453.note: Replaces Markup() with html.escape() at the point the untrusted label is embedded; correct output encoding, no other behavior change.

R454.note: ValidAlgorithms pinned to HmacSha256 matches the SymmetricSecurityKey already in use, closing algorithm confusion without narrowing legitimate token acceptance.

R455.note: Straightforward bounds check before the array access; preserves existing error-return convention.

R456.note: subtle.ConstantTimeCompare plus the retained empty-string guard exactly reproduces the stated contract (exact match only, false otherwise).

R457.note: Only rejects URIs with a non-null scheme; verified against OpenJDK 26 that new URI("//evil.com/path") has scheme=null but host=evil.com, so protocol-relative redirects (//evil.com/...) bypass this check entirely -- vector only partially closed.

R458.note: archive/tar swap correctly eliminates the shell sink entirely, but the ctx parameter is now unused, silently dropping the contract's required request-context cancellation for long-running reads -- not mentioned in the write-up.

R459.note: shared_ptr/weak_ptr with lock()-before-invoke is the standard fix for this dangling-observer pattern; order and live-observer-only invocation are preserved as required.

R460.note: _escape_inline_arg only escapes backslash and double-quote characters, never the literal CR/LF bytes; Redis's inline-command framing splits on the first raw newline in the byte stream before any quote parsing runs, so the exact CRLF injection the write-up's own worked example describes still succeeds against the 'fixed' code.

R461.note: Correct SecureRandom replacement with the predictable seed discarded; seedParam/seed become unused dead code, a minor cleanliness nit but no behavior change.
